title: Worked journey: A ward councillor’s question, routed

blocks.label: Definition
blocks.html: This section runs one question through the whole method, in the order real work uses it. A councillor asks whether two local schemes will bring obesity down in the ward. You split the question into its parts and mark each one inside or outside what you can assess, by the five signals. You answer the part that is yours. You name an owner for each other part, send each a five-part question, and judge each reply with the five checks. You enter each owner in your contact list. Then, in public, you say what you can answer, the public sentence, and who can answer the rest. The section ends on what the replies do not settle.

blocks.label: In plain terms
blocks.html:
This section uses no new tool.

The case has seven steps.

  1. A councillor asks a question, and you hear it as it was asked.
  2. You split the question into parts, mark each as inside or outside what you can assess, and answer the part that is yours.
  3. You name the owner of each part that is not yours.
  4. You write each owner a question in five parts.
  5. You judge each reply with the five checks, and you ask back when a check fails.
  6. You enter each owner in your contact list.
  7. In public, you say what you can answer, the public sentence, and who can answer the rest.

The case runs over two meetings and four weeks. Routing takes days, so this book’s rule is to start it the day the question is asked.

blocks.label: Illustration 1
blocks.html:
Step 1. The question. Wards Committees are set up in a municipality of 3,00,000 (three lakh) people or more (Article 243S of the Constitution, https://indiacode.gov.in/handle/123456789/618394). Where a committee covers one ward, the ward’s own member of the municipality chairs it. Now the meeting.

A made-up meeting, 11 Dec 2026: the Wards Committee of a municipal corporation. The councillor is in the chair, and you attend as the community medicine resident the corporation asked for health advice. The councillor asks: “The corporation is building a cycle lane on the main road, and the government Ayurveda college has offered a weight-loss camp in the ward. Will these two bring obesity down here?”

Step 2. Recognise. The councillor named two schemes. The question holds a third part that nobody said aloud: how the ward would know whether obesity changed. Split the question into its three parts, and mark each one inside or past your edge.

Part of the question Inside or past your edge Signal
Will the cycle lane bring obesity down here? past About to act, with No test
Will the camp bring obesity down here? past About to act, with Unknown standard
How would the ward know whether obesity changed? inside none

Take the rows one at a time. The lane: the committee will tell residents what to expect, and may press the corporation on the lane’s design, so About to act fires. Behind it, No test: you cannot say what result, on this ward’s streets, would show a yes or a no wrong. The camp: About to act again. Behind it, Unknown standard: you do not know Ayurveda’s standard references or methods, so you could not check any answer you gave. The hidden part is yours: measuring whether obesity changes is community medicine.

Now say the part you can answer, inside the same meeting.

“I can answer one part now. If the committee wants to know whether obesity changes in the ward, we measure adults before the lane opens and the camp begins, and again later, in the same way. I can design that with the health department. Whether the lane will get people walking and cycling, and what the camp will do for the people who go, are the other two parts. That is outside what I can assess, and here is who can: the municipal town-planning office for the lane, and a qualified Ayush practitioner for the camp. I will put the questions to them tomorrow and bring their answers to the next meeting.”

That is the public sentence, in its exact words, then the owners, then the next step. You will say it again at the next meeting, with what the owners said.

Step 3. Name the owners. Each part that is not yours has an owner this book has already named.

For the lane, urban planning is among the matters the Constitution’s Twelfth Schedule lists for a State’s law to give to municipalities (Article 243W). Its first item is “Urban planning including town planning”. Roads are another: “Roads and bridges”. The owner is the municipal town-planning office, and through it an urban or transport planner. The planner owns the street half: what would make the streets walkable and cyclable, and whether residents are likely to use the lane. What more walking and cycling would do to obesity is not the planner’s question. Its owner is people who study physical activity in communities, and step 7 says where this course teaches that evidence.

For the camp, the owner is a qualified Ayush practitioner. The nearest is the Ayush medical officer at a primary health centre where Ayush is co-located. The Ministry of Ayush’s Annual Report 2024-25 (https://ayush.gov.in/assets/pdf/annualReport/Annual-Report24-25_English.pdf) says the Government of India places Ayush facilities in PHCs, CHCs and district hospitals, “thus expanding choices of the patients”. It adds that the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare supports the engagement of Ayush doctors there. The other possible owner is a teacher at the college’s own hospital.

Because the college is a government college, the State’s Ayush directorate stands behind it. Chhattisgarh’s directorate (https://cgayush.admissions.nic.in/cg-ayush/, as its portal read on 9 Oct 2026) is one example. It gives its primary responsibility as making infrastructure, equipment, drugs and other essentials available to run the government colleges and hospitals. You ask the Ayush medical officer first, because a practitioner can answer for what a system offers a patient; the directorate equips and staffs colleges and hospitals, and is not who you ask about this camp’s evidence.

blocks.label: Where this picture breaks
blocks.html: Splitting the question works because each part has a different owner. If the councillor had asked only how the ward would know whether obesity changed, there would be nothing to route: the whole question would be yours. And a part is not yours just because it mentions obesity; the lane and the camp are questions about a street and a system of medicine.

blocks.label: Illustration 2
blocks.html:
Step 4. Write the questions. The curriculum this book follows gives both questions in these words. Each sits in its Question row unchanged, with one line saying what “this ward” and “this patient” mean here.

To the municipal town-planning office, sent 12 Dec 2026:

Part Your question
Decision At its meeting on 8 Jan 2027, the Wards Committee decides what to tell residents about the cycle lane on the main road, and whether to ask the corporation for anything more before work starts. The councillor is waiting for my advice.
Context The corporation is building the lane on the ward’s main road. The committee has asked whether it will bring obesity down. I can measure obesity in the ward; I cannot judge street design. I have not seen the lane’s drawings.
Question “what would make this ward’s streets walkable and cyclable for the least active, and which plan or budget does that sit in?” Here, the ward is ours, and the lane on the main road is the first thing to look at.
Form A short list of what would make the most difference, the lane included, each with the plan and the budget it sits in. Tell me how sure you are on each, and on what; I cannot judge the designs.
Deadline By 1 Jan 2027, a week before the meeting. If it comes later, the committee discusses the lane without it.

To the Ayush medical officer at the co-located PHC, sent 12 Dec 2026:

Part Your question
Decision At its meeting on 8 Jan 2027, the Wards Committee decides whether to welcome the government Ayurveda college’s weight-loss camp in the ward, and what to tell residents about it. The councillor is waiting for my advice.
Context The college has offered a weight-loss camp for the ward’s residents. I do not know what the camp will provide. Some residents who may come take tablets for diabetes from the urban primary health centre. I cannot judge Ayurveda’s methods or its standard references.
Question “what does this system offer this patient for weight, on what evidence, and what does it interact with in the treatment they already have?” Here, “this patient” is each resident who comes to the camp, and above all those already taking tablets from the centre.
Form What the camp will give each resident; the evidence, with references; and, for residents on tablets, what the camp will check and who will be told. Tell me how sure you are on each, and on what; I cannot judge the methods.
Deadline By 1 Jan 2027, a week before the meeting. If it comes later, the committee decides about the camp without it.

Step 5. Judge the replies. Start with the reply that fails.

A made-up reply, 22 Dec 2026, from the Ayush medical officer: “Thank you for writing. Ayurveda is one of the Ayush systems, with its own colleges, such as the one offering the camp, and its own way of assessing each person, including advice on diet and daily routine. The college’s teachers are experienced, and I am sure the camp will be well run. You are welcome to visit our centre on any weekday.”

Run the five checks and mark them.

Check Your mark Your reason
Asked fails It answers “what is Ayurveda?”, a neighbouring question. It says nothing about this camp or these residents.
How sure fails “I am sure the camp will be well run” is about the running of the camp, and rests on nothing stated. On the camp’s evidence, it says nothing.
Own field passes It stays inside the system it describes.
References fails It gives none, and How sure names nothing it rests on.
Decision fails It neither changes nor confirms what you will tell the committee, because it answered another question.

Asked, How sure and References fail, and your own Decision row is clear, so you ask back. References fails only because the reply cites nothing and names no basis, so the ask-back covers it. Write to the same owner, quote your Question row, and name what is missing.

A made-up ask-back, 23 Dec 2026, to the Ayush medical officer: “Thank you. My question was: ‘what does this system offer this patient for weight, on what evidence, and what does it interact with in the treatment they already have?’, for the residents who come to the college’s camp. Your reply tells me about Ayurveda in general. What is missing: what this camp will give each resident; the evidence, with its references; how sure you are, and on what; and, for residents taking diabetes tablets from the centre, what the camp will check and who will be told.”

Now the reply that passes.

A made-up reply, 29 Dec 2026, from the municipal town-planning office: “Three things would matter most for the least active in your ward. First, footpaths that run without breaks, and are kept free of stalls and parked vehicles, on the roads to the market and the school. Second, safe crossings on the main road. Third, the cycle lane, if residents can reach it safely from the lanes where they live. The cycle lane is in the corporation’s road-works budget for this year. The footpaths and crossings are in no plan yet; they would have to be proposed for next year’s budget. We are sure of where each one sits, because we hold those documents. We are less sure that residents will use the lane. The National Urban Transport Policy says that many cycle tracks and pedestrian paths ‘do not get used as initially envisaged’, and asks for open debate on their designs ‘with experts and the community that is expected to use them’ (paragraph 29). Whether walking and cycling more would change obesity in the ward is not ours to say; the health department would know how to measure it.”

Check Your mark Your reason
Asked passes It says what would make the streets walkable and cyclable for the least active, and which plan or budget each sits in.
How sure passes Sure of where each item sits, on the documents the office holds; less sure that residents will use the lane, on the national policy’s own words.
Own field passes It names what lies outside its field, whether obesity would change, and who can measure it.
References passes Open the National Urban Transport Policy and find paragraph 29: both quoted phrases are there, and they say what the reply says.
Decision passes It changes your advice: the committee can ask for footpaths and crossings in next year’s budget, and for an open debate on the lane’s design with residents.

The policy is at https://mohua.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/10/0da700a8b86f2faee310bd49592ee99a.pdf. Checking the reference is Book 0’s four acts in one line: find it, confirm it, find the passage, read it. Goldman’s first commandment, for the person who answers, is that “the consultant should determine the question that is being asked” (the owner, in the paper’s word). This reply did.

Last, the second Ayush reply.

A made-up reply, 30 Dec 2026, from the Ayush medical officer: “The college will hold the camp on three Saturdays at our centre, which serves your ward; I host it, so I answer for it. Each resident sees a teacher from the college, who records their weight and waist, asks about their diet, daily routine and any medicines, and gives advice on diet and daily routine. Some will be offered yoga sessions at the centre, and some may be given an Ayurvedic medicine. The camp follows the college’s written protocol, which lists the studies it relies on; I attach it. I cannot tell you whether residents of this ward will lose weight, or how much: that has not been measured here, and I would want the protocol’s studies judged by someone who can judge them. Anyone who takes tablets for diabetes will be asked to bring them. The camp will not change them. The protocol lists every medicine the camp may give, and the camp will write down any it gives, so that the doctor at the centre who prescribes the tablets can check each one against them. Whether the camp changes obesity in the ward is for whoever measures it; you said that would be the health department.”

Check Your mark Your reason
Asked passes It says what this camp gives these residents and on what evidence, and, on what it interacts with, lists every medicine it may give for the prescribing doctor to check.
How sure passes It says what it cannot tell you (whether residents here will lose weight) and why: not measured here.
Own field passes It names what lies outside: judging the studies, and measuring change in the ward.
References passes You open the attached protocol (made up) and find each study it lists: each exists, and each passage the protocol cites says what the protocol says it says. You do not judge the studies’ methods, and this check says nothing about whether the camp works.
Decision passes It confirms what you will tell the committee: what the camp offers, that its effect on weight here is not known, and how residents on tablets are kept safe.

Responsive does not mean right. It means the reply is usable for the decision; whether the studies’ methods are sound is a second owner’s question, if the committee needs it judged.

Step 6. The contact list. Two rows go into your list.

Field Owner Name and institution How you know them Last question asked Asked on Checked on
Urban and transport planning an urban or transport planner; the municipal town-planning office the town-planning officer, the municipal corporation worked with what would make this ward’s streets walkable and cyclable for the least active, and which plan or budget that sits in 12 Dec 2026 8 Jan 2027
Ayush systems a qualified Ayush practitioner; for the State’s arrangements, the State’s Ayush directorate the Ayush medical officer, co-located PHC worked with what the college’s camp gives residents for weight, on what evidence, and what it does for those on diabetes tablets 23 Dec 2026 8 Jan 2027

Both say worked with, because you asked each a question and used the reply. The Ayush row’s Asked on is the date you asked back, because that was the last question.

blocks.label: Where this picture breaks
blocks.html: Both replies came on time and from people willing to answer. A reply may not come, or may come after the meeting; then you tell the committee what you asked, of whom, and when you expect it, and you do not answer in the owner’s place. And a responsive reply is still only as good as the references behind it, which you can find and read but not judge.

blocks.label: Illustration 3
blocks.html:
Step 7. What you say, in public.

A made-up meeting, 8 Jan 2027: the Wards Committee again. The councillor asks, “So, will these two bring obesity down here?”

You say: “There are three parts to that. One is mine. We can know whether obesity changes in the ward: we measure adults now, before the lane opens and the camp begins, and again in the same way a year later. That will show whether it changed, not which of the two changed it. Whether the lane will get our least active residents walking and cycling, and what the camp will do for the people who go, are the other two parts. That is outside what I can assess, and here is who can. The town-planning office has told us what would make our streets walkable, and where the money for each part sits. The Ayush medical officer at the health centre has told us what the camp gives each resident, and how residents on diabetes tablets are kept safe. I suggest we invite them both to the next meeting.”

Book 24, Physical activity and sedentary behaviour science, teaches what the evidence on physical activity and weight shows. This book does not. Notice that the public sentence appears again, in its exact words, and the two owners follow it at once.

Now read what the replies do not settle. Neither reply says whether obesity in the ward will fall, and neither owner claimed to know. The before-and-after measure will show whether obesity changed, not what changed it: the lane, the camp and everything else in the ward change at the same time. Nothing in this journey judged the lane’s design or Ayurveda’s methods; both stayed with their owners. The planning reply rests on paragraph 29 of a 2006 policy that you checked says what the reply says; whether residents of this ward will use this lane is still unknown.

blocks.label: Where this picture breaks
blocks.html: This case had two owners who could be reached and a committee that could wait four weeks. When the committee must decide at once, say the part you can answer and the public sentence, name the owners, and ask the committee to decide only what does not depend on their replies.

points.html: In a committee, split the question into its parts before you answer any of it. Answer the part that is yours, route the rest, and say aloud which is which.

A before-and-after measure in one ward shows whether obesity changed, not which of the things that changed at the same time caused it. Say so when you offer it, or the committee will hear a promise you cannot keep.
A reply that describes a system, an office or a plan in general has answered a neighbouring question. Ask back, in writing, quoting your Question row and naming what is missing, before the meeting.
When residents on prescribed tablets may join any camp, ask what the camp will check and who will be told, and keep the doctor who prescribes the tablets informed.
Nothing in this case judged the lane’s design or Ayurveda’s methods; both stayed with their owners.

blocks.prompt: From memory: list the seven steps of this case in order, with one line each.
blocks.answer: 1. The question as asked. 2. Recognise: split it, mark each part inside or outside, name the signals; answer your part. 3. Name the owner of each outside part. 4. Write each owner a five-part question. 5. Judge each reply with the five checks; ask back when Asked, How sure or Own field fails. 6. Enter each owner in the contact list. 7. In public: say what you can answer, the public sentence, and who can answer the rest.

blocks.prompt: A made-up line from a member at the first meeting: “Cycling burns fat, so the lane will bring obesity down. And the camp can’t do any harm, so let it run.” Name the signals that should have stopped the speaker, and rewrite the line.
blocks.answer: For the lane: About to act with No test — the speaker cannot say what result in this ward would show the claim wrong. For the camp: About to act with Unknown standard — “can’t do any harm” is a judgement about a system of medicine whose standard the speaker does not know. Rewrite: “That is outside what I can assess, and here is who can: whether the lane will get people cycling is a question for the town-planning office, and what the camp offers is a question for an Ayush practitioner. Let’s ask them both, and measure obesity in the ward before and after.”

blocks.prompt: A made-up addition at the next meeting: the corporation will pay for hoardings in the ward to announce the camp, and will place the order on 20 Jan 2027. The councillor asks, “Will people actually see them?” Write the question in five parts, and say to whom it goes.
blocks.answer:
“Will people see them?” asks about reach, so it goes to a communications or social-marketing agency, with a copy to the State IEC officer. What hoardings do to what people buy or do would be a marketing scientist’s question instead. Here is the question.

Part Your question
Decision Whether the corporation spends its sum on hoardings for the camp, or on another way of telling residents. The councillor is waiting; the order is placed on 20 Jan 2027.
Context Residents of one ward, adults. Hoardings for the three camp Saturdays. The aim is that residents know the camp’s dates and place.
Question “what reach and frequency will this budget buy in this audience, and how will exposure be measured?”
Form An estimated reach and frequency for the hoardings over the weeks before the camp, with the source of each, and how exposure will be counted. Tell me how sure you are and on what; I cannot judge your method.
Deadline By 15 Jan 2027, before the order is placed on 20 Jan. If it comes later, the hoardings are ordered without it.

blocks.prompt: A third made-up reply arrives, from a colleague at the college: “Our camps are always popular, and our teachers are very experienced. I am confident this camp will be a success.” Run the five checks, and say what you do next.
blocks.answer:
Check Your mark Your reason
Asked fails Popularity and experience were not asked about.
How sure fails It states confidence, and gives nothing it rests on.
Own field fails “A success” leaves unsaid what lies outside the college’s field: whether obesity changes in the ward.
References fails None given, and How sure names no basis.
Decision fails It neither changes nor confirms your advice.

Checks 1 to 4 fail; References fails only because none are given and no basis is named, so one ask-back covers all four, quoting your Question row. Confidence is not a reason to accept a reply: the section on improvising showed confidence that did not follow accuracy.

blocks.prompt: Audience: a journalist. Three minutes, no jargon, one quotable sentence. After the second meeting, a reporter from a Hindi daily asks you: “Will the cycle lane fix obesity in the ward?” Answer in three minutes, with one sentence they can quote.
blocks.answer: Say what you can: the ward will measure adults’ weight and waist now and again a year later, which will show whether obesity changed but not what changed it. Then the sentence, in its exact words: “That is outside what I can assess, and here is who can.” Then the owner: the town-planning office has told the committee what would make the ward’s streets walkable, and whether residents will use the lane is still unknown. Quotable sentence: “We will know whether obesity changes in the ward because we will measure it; whether the lane gets people cycling is a question for the planners, and they have told us what else the streets need.”
